one_liner: Vantel builds AI software for commercial insurance brokerages. Its Y Combinator participation warrants a look, but a reported seed round makes first-round outreach unlikely.

top_signals.signal: Vantel is listed in Y Combinator’s 2025–2026 European cohort.
Vantel reportedly raised a $2 million seed round in March 2025 from Y Combinator, Inception Fund, Rebel Fund and angel investors.

Model score 84.5 of 100 (at the top of the reference cohort). The fintech and deep-tech tags, YC participation and a co-founder in the CTO role lifted the score. The model also flagged a technical founder, selective school backgrounds and study abroad; the founder records list institutions but do not independently confirm those flags.

team: Love Redin is co-founder and CEO; his record lists KTH Royal Institute of Technology. Ulme Wennberg is co-founder and CTO; his record lists KTH, Stockholm School of Economics and the University of Washington. The CTO role is recorded, but neither founder record confirms the model’s technical-founder flag.
why_early: Unknown whether the reported March 2025 seed round was priced. The round was already reported, so Vantel should not be treated as a pre-first-funding lead.
devils_advocate_risks: Established brokers may resist integrating AI into existing workflows.
Supporting different insurance products and regulatory requirements across regions may complicate expansion.
next_step: HTGF Industrial Tech team: Ask the founders whether the reported March 2025 seed round was priced equity.
